articles.title: US proposes ending H-1B deference policy
articles.summary: The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has proposed ending a policy that generally allows immigration officers to rely on earlier approvals when reviewing certain visa extensions. The change could lead to fresh scrutiny of H-1B petitions, more document requests and higher costs for employers.What is the proposed change?The proposal would remove a rule that asks US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) officers to generally respect earlier eligibility decisions when the same parties and facts remain unchanged.Also Read: US ends 540-day automatic work permit extension for immigrants: What changes nowUnder the current policy, officers generally rely on an earlier approval when considering an extension if the circumstances remain the same. They can depart from that decision if they find a significant error, a major change in circumstances or new information that affects eligibility.If the proposal takes effect, officers could reassess each extension request even when the circumstances have not changed. Employers would need to establish that workers continue to meet the requirements for their visa category.Why could H-1B workers be affected?H-1B workers seeking to extend their stay in the US could face closer scrutiny of their petitions. Employers may have to provide additional documents to establish that their employees remain eligible.Also Read: Bahrain’s 90-day temporary work rule explained: What Indian expats need to knowDHS said the existing policy could limit officers' ability to examine cases fully and identify errors or possible fraud. The department said removing the requirement would strengthen checks and ensure employers continue to prove that their workers qualify for the requested immigration benefit.The change could affect H-1B workers from India and other countries, as well as their employers, by subjecting extension petitions to fresh scrutiny. Workers could face additional document requests and delays if USCIS seeks further evidence to verify their eligibility.More paperwork and costs for employersDHS estimates that the change could lead to 6,044 additional requests for evidence (RFEs) each year and cost petitioners about $133,987 annually.An RFE is a notice from USCIS asking an employer or applicant to provide more documents or information before the agency decides a case. Responding to such a notice can increase the time and work involved in an application.The department also warned that more detailed reviews could lengthen processing times and create uncertainty for workers seeking to continue their employment in the US. Additional reviews could increase USCIS's workload and put pressure on its processing resources.The proposed change applies to Form I-129, which employers use to petition for non-immigrant workers. The form covers H-1B petitions as well as several other worker visa categories.The proposal is not a final rule and has not taken effect. DHS is accepting public comments until November 13, 2026, and will consider the feedback before making a final decision.

articles.summary: RIYADH, - The Saudi-led military coalition in Yemen said on Thursday that the country's Houthis had attempted to attack dozens of Saudi airports, ports and oil facilities, as fighting between the Iran-aligned group and Saudi Arabia intensified.The Houthis have been firing ballistic missiles and drones at key Saudi sites for a week, in response to the kingdom's backing of government forces in Yemen's renewed civil war. The coalition's latest statement highlighted the risk to Saudi civilian infrastructure as the conflict escalated.Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki said at a press conference that the Houthis had launched 20 attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh this month, killing 17 people and wounding 333 others. The airport, one of Saudi Arabia's main international aviation hubs, was among the civilian infrastructure targeted in what the coalition described as a series of attacks.The coalition also said Houthi attacks on Abha airport, in southwestern Saudi Arabia near the Yemeni border, had killed three people and wounded 28.Maliki said the Houthis had acquired advanced military technology with the help of "regional actors," including ballistic missiles, drones and explosive-laden fast boats.The spokesperson also said the coalition had destroyed 127 weapons storage facilities and launch platforms in Yemen's mountainous areas.He called on the Houthis to immediately halt operations targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure, and said the group should read the coalition's statement carefully and "between the lines."Shortly after the coalition's statement, the Houthi military spokesperson said Saudi airspace and airports were unsafe, renewing a warning to airlines while excluding airspace over the holy cities of Mecca and Medina.Yemen has been mired in conflict since the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa in 2014, prompting a Saudi-led military intervention the following year. The UN-brokered truce in 2022 largely halted major fighting, and a de facto truce held even after it expired six months later. But efforts to turn it into a lasting political settlement have stalled as regional tensions have intensified.

articles.title: Current account deficit narrows to $5.2 billion in August: RBI data

India's current account deficit narrowed to USD 5.2 billion in August from USD 6.1 billion a year ago, aided by a lower merchandise trade deficit and higher surpluses in services trade, according to preliminary data released by the RBI on Thursday.
The net deficit in the merchandise trade account declined to USD 26.6 billion in August from USD 27.6 billion in the same month last year.
Merchandise exports rose to USD 44.7 billion in August from USD 35.1 billion a year ago, while imports increased to USD 71.3 billion from USD 62.7 billion, the RBI data showed.
The surplus in services trade increased to USD 16.5 billion in August from USD 15.6 billion a year ago. Services exports rose to USD 35.5 billion from USD 31.2 billion, while imports increased to USD 18.9 billion from USD 15.6 billion.
Net transfers, including remittances, increased to USD 12.8 billion in August from USD 12.2 billion a year ago, while the net deficit in the income account widened to USD 8 billion from USD 6.3 .

articles.title: Reliance Jio’s next big bet is beyond data
articles.summary: IPO-bound Reliance Jio is looking to go beyond data connectivity by partnering with technology companies to create new markets, rather than simply distribute their products, Akash Ambani revealed on Thursday, citing the telecom operator’s collaboration with Google on its artificial intelligence service Gemini.“This is not a simple distribution deal,” Ambani, Jio platforms' Managing Director, said at Jio’s IPO press conference, explaining how the partnership had helped create a market for Google’s flagship AI product in India.Also read: Jio IPO: With tech muscle, Akash Ambani makes $1.4 tn digital economy pitchGoogle already has a significant presence in India, with more than a billion users across each of its platforms, and Gemini as its flagship product. Yet the company partnered with Jio, Ambani said, drawing a parallel with how the telecom operator had approached the data market.“What we were able to do, like we did with the data market, was co-create a new market,” he said.The partnership has since resulted in Gemini adding 13 million new subscribers to its paid service, Ambani said, pointing to the opportunity Jio sees in working with technology companies beyond conventional connectivity.Jio eyes share of $1.4 trillion digital economyAmbani said Jio Platforms aims to capture a significant share of India's projected $1.4 trillion digital economy by FY31, citing its technology capabilities and end-to-end technology stack."We see $1.4 trillion digital economy by FY31. The end-to-end stack gives us the ability to capture a large market share for this," he said.The technology-led growth strategy is central to Jio's pitch to investors ahead of its public listing, as the company looks to expand digital services, technology platforms and enterprise businesses alongside its telecom operations.Ambani said Jio had filed 7,200 patents so far, placing it among the world's leading companies in patent filings. "We are the only Indian company among top 20 global companies in terms of patents filed. 7200 patents filed till now for Jio," he said.5G network and global partnershipsAmbani also pointed to Jio's network reach and pricing as advantages in expanding access to digital services across India."Mission of Jio is connect every Indian home to highest order of digital services. We are the largest 5G base outside China. Our pricing per GB is the lowest anywhere in the world," he said.Jio has expanded beyond mobile connectivity into home broadband, entertainment, cloud services, enterprise technology and artificial intelligence. Its subscriber base stood at about 533 million at the end of June 2026, providing a potential customer base for additional digital offerings."Some of the biggest global tech companies like Google have partnered with us," Ambani said. Google holds a 7.73% stake in Jio Platforms, while Meta owns about 9.98%. Both were among the investors that backed the company during its 2020 fundraising exercise.Also read: Marine Drive was lit up for Reliance IPO: Uday Kotak recalls Dhirubhai Ambani’s legacyJio IPO: Price band, issue size and datesJio Platforms has set a price band of Rs 1,065-1,119 per share for its IPO, which opens on October 21 and closes on October 23. The anchor investor book opens on October 19, with listing expected on October 28.The company plans to issue up to 27 crore fresh equity shares, raising as much as Rs 30,213 crore at the upper end of the price band. At that price, the offering values Jio Platforms at about Rs 10.3 lakh crore, or roughly $108 billion.The IPO could surpass Hyundai Motor India's Rs 27,900 crore issue in 2024 to become India's largest public offering. It will comprise an entirely fresh issue, with no offer for sale by existing shareholders.Jio has also reserved shares worth up to Rs 2,500 crore for eligible Reliance Industries shareholders and Rs 500 crore for eligible employees. Retail investors can apply for a minimum of 12 shares, requiring Rs 13,428 at the upper end of the price band.

articles.title: SIR storm reaches the Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court issued a notice to the Election Commission of India over the plea by Rahul Gandhi and other opposition members over mass voter deletions and alleged irregularities in the revision of voter rolls exercise.The country's top court is seeking response from the Election Commission of India, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi on Gandhi and others' plea.Also Read: SC likely to hear Rahul Gandhi, INDIA bloc leader’s plea against ECI’s SIR decisions tomorrowIt is hearing a plea on which challenges India's controversial revision in voter roles, as the opposition bloc looks to suspend the exercise and hold the top election official accountable after series of mass protests and detentions.The apex court is also hearing multiple petitions pertaining to detention of protestors by the Delhi Police, alleged brutality and multiple restrictions of free travel and movement in the national capital. It will also be scrutinising the detention of multiple Supreme Court lawyers and journalists, along with a curb on internet usage in cenral Delhi over the last weekend.SC's notice to Election Commission over RaGa's pleaThe top court issued notice on a petition filed by Gandhi and nine other INDIA bloc leaders challenging the revision of electoral rolls.A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi remarked while issuing notice, “We would also ask one of the petitioners about his conduct.” The bench sought response from ECI, CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi on Gandhi and others' plea.The petition follows an Opposition march towards the Supreme Court on October 12, led by Gandhi, against the SIR exercise.A quick background checkThe expected hearing comes on the heels of massive protests led by India's opposition political parties and youth-led outfit Cockroach Janata Party after a report by the Indian Express alleged Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar authorised decisions without the consent of other Election Commissioners and disregarded their objections regarding the Special Intensive Revision of Electoral Rolls.The SIR exercise, launched in 2025, has led to more than 13 crore names being removed from draft voter lists. Opposition parties have alleged that eligible voters are being left out to aide the interests of the ruling BJP.The Election Commission and the BJP have defended the SIR exercise saying that the move is to ensure voter rolls remain transparent and not have names of deceased, duplicate or inelligible voters. The Opposition has called for the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar and for independent probes into the working of the poll body. The BJP has criticised the opposition parties, saying they have lost elections due to poor leadership and rejection from voters rather than due to the SIR process.India is gearing up for key electoral battles next year with special focus on Uttar Pradesh, the country's most populous state.
